hints: Use $P = F_{\text{D}} \times v$ to find the driving force in both situations: on the horizontal road ($P = 36\text{ kW}, v = 18\text{ m s}^{-1}$) and up the hill ($P = 21\text{ kW}, v = 12\text{ m s}^{-1}$).
On the horizontal road at steady speed, the driving force equals the resistance: $F_{\text{D}1} = 18A + B$.
Up the hill at steady speed, the driving force equals resistance plus the down-slope component of weight: $F_{\text{D}2} = (12A + B) + mg\sin\theta$.
Solve the resulting two simultaneous linear equations for $A$ and $B$.
walkthrough:
Find the driving force on the horizontal road at steady speed $v = 18\text{ m s}^{-1}$ with power $36\text{ kW} = 36\,000\text{ W}$:
$$F_{\text{D}1} = \frac{P}{v} = \frac{36\,000}{18} = 2000\text{ N}$$

Equate driving force to resistance $R = 18A + B$ for horizontal motion at steady speed ($a = 0$):
$$18A + B = 2000$$

Find the driving force up the hill at steady speed $v = 12\text{ m s}^{-1}$ with power $21\text{ kW} = 21\,000\text{ W}$:
$$F_{\text{D}2} = \frac{P}{v} = \frac{21\,000}{12} = 1750\text{ N}$$

Equate driving force to resistance plus the weight component with $m = 1000\text{ kg}$ and $\sin\theta = 0.05$:
$$1750 = (12A + B) + 1000(10)(0.05) = (12A + B) + 500$$
$$12A + B = 1750 - 500 = 1250$$

Subtract the second equation from the first to solve for $A$ and $B$:
$$(18A + B) - (12A + B) = 2000 - 1250$$
$$6A = 750 \implies A = 125$$
$$B = 2000 - 18(125) = 2000 - 2250 = -250$$
teacher_walkthrough: Recall that when a vehicle moves at constant steady speed ($a = 0$), the forward driving force produced by the engine must exactly balance the total opposing forces along the direction of motion.

Situation 1: Motion along a horizontal road.
Calculate the driving force $F_{\text{D}1}$ using $P = F_{\text{D}} v$ with $P = 36\,000\text{ W}$ and $v = 18\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$F_{\text{D}1} = \frac{P}{v} = \frac{36\,000}{18} = 2000\text{ N}$$
Because the road is horizontal, the only opposing force is resistance $R = Av + B$ evaluated at $v = 18\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$18A + B = 2000 \quad \text{--- (Equation 1)}$$

Situation 2: Motion up an inclined hill.
Calculate the driving force $F_{\text{D}2}$ with $P = 21\,000\text{ W}$ and $v = 12\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$F_{\text{D}2} = \frac{P}{v} = \frac{21\,000}{12} = 1750\text{ N}$$
Along the incline, the opposing forces are the resistance $R = 12A + B$ and the downward component of weight $mg\sin\theta$:
$$W_{\parallel} = mg\sin\theta = 1000 \times 10 \times 0.05 = 500\text{ N}$$
Set the driving force equal to the total resistance:
$$1750 = (12A + B) + 500$$
Subtract $500$ from both sides:
$$12A + B = 1250 \quad \text{--- (Equation 2)}$$

Solve the linear system of Equations 1 and 2 simultaneously:
Subtract Equation 2 from Equation 1:
$$(18A + B) - (12A + B) = 2000 - 1250$$
$$6A = 750$$
Divide by $6$:
$$A = \frac{750}{6} = 125$$
Substitute $A = 125$ into Equation 1:
$$18(125) + B = 2000$$
$$2250 + B = 2000$$
Subtract $2250$ from both sides:
$$B = 2000 - 2250 = -250$$
Thus $A = 125$ and $B = -250$.
